reason: The named characters explicitly identified in this Genesis 41 passage are: Pharaoh (the Egyptian king), Joseph (a Hebrew slave who interprets dreams and becomes elevated to power), Asenath (the daughter of Potiphera, a priest of On), and Potiphera (a priest). None of these individuals can be classified as 'regular people' — Pharaoh is a monarch, Joseph despite his initial enslavement is portrayed with special wisdom and divine favor, and Asenath and Potiphera are from the priestly class. While other individuals are mentioned (magicians, wise men, the chief butler, the chief baker), they are not given individual names. The only named characters in the text all possess some form of elevated status or special significance.
